Replay

Author scenes and replayable gameplay in Scrapyard

5 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Start in the editorScene mapComposed gameplay state and rulesChange appearance, definitions, or gameplay rulesIdentities, input, and recoveryProcedural rendering and specialized pathsValidation

Scrapyard shows the recommended separation between authored Godot composition and replayable Odin gameplay. The original sibling Scrapyard remains independently runnable. This example uses authority/prediction/observed presentation; use Duel for deterministic peer rollback and Slopball for cooperative engine physics.

Start in the editor#

Build the project with the repository's normal Odin/Godot build workflow, then open project.godot in Godot. The project plugin also rebuilds script bindings as needed.

Shell
nix develop --command bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/replay_scrapyard
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh

The following scenes run independently with F6. Here, runner means the player character; the Replay runner is the runtime advancing simulation. The enemy, runner, and HUD view previews create no Session or World. The gameplay workbench runs a real game session:

Scene Try changing What owns the change
dev/enemy_view.tscn Preview-state Resource, Body offset, style tint/texture/fps, Telegraph color Enemy scene, preview and appearance Resources
dev/runner_view.tscn Preview down/reload, Gun/Flash offsets, Reload/Beacon origins Runner scene and composed weapon/equipment scripts
dev/hud_view.tscn Vitals layout, labels/theme, HUD anchors Authored HUD scene with sample display values
dev/workbench.tscn Hurt/jam/statuses, boss, kegs, shop The real game, driven through admitted development actions

The standalone view previews are cosmetic inspection tools. The workbench tests gameplay and multiplayer-facing behavior through the actual runner. They serve different editing tasks, and neither writes arbitrary live World fields.

Scene map#

Text
entities/mob.tscn                 ScrapEnemyView
  Body                           authored Sprite2D
  Telegraph                      views/components/telegraph.tscn
visuals/enemies/*.tres            ScrapEnemyStyle Resources
archetypes/enemies/*.tres         MobDef + scene + appearance registrations

entities/runner.tscn              ScrapRunnerView
  Body                           authored Sprite2D
  Gun                            views/components/weapon.tscn
    Flash                        authored child atlas/offset
  Reload                         views/components/reload.tscn
  Beacon                         views/components/beacon.tscn
  Nameplate                      authored Label/layout

ui/hud.tscn                      ReplayScrapyardHud
  Vitals, Ammo, BossPlate, Prompt authored UI layout

scripts/views owns the actors' local appearance and process callbacks. Weapon flashes and equipment bob/pulse are reusable child behaviors. Geometry, textures, origins and tuning live in scenes/Resources. Scripts capture authored origins before animating relative to them; ordinary scene composition survives the runtime binding.

shared/presentation owns pure projection into Mob_View, Runner_View and Hud_View. These contain bounded values without scene or mutable Resource pointers. scripts/mob_bridge.odin uses an owned typed script/archetype binding and forwards local impact notices through a typed visitor. Generated view descriptors select the explicit hooks; a shared scope tracker compares the explicit run/floor key. drawing.odin selects the timelines, applies smoothing, and supplies runner/HUD values. View components select actor frames and animate equipment.

The Stormcaller walkthrough records adding a new enemy through this path, including the actual authoring glue and save-version work it required.

Composed gameplay state and rules#

shared/game/game.odin defines the snapshot boundary and Player's composed state: Gun_State, revive Channel, effect slots, cooldowns, progression and motion values. combat.odin, brains.odin, abilities.odin, effects.odin and the shared replay/play mechanisms contain rules. Node animation never determines a hit. The small component recipe demonstrates composing state and procedures without a scene, ECS or new framework registration layer.

Keep mutable gameplay state here, including RNG and allocation/lifetime state. Keep visual timers, cached child references and particle resources in view scripts. The framework handles replay/history/transport; the game continues to choose its prediction, authority, admission and recovery policies.

Change appearance, definitions, or gameplay rules#

For a new look for an existing enemy, duplicate a Resource in visuals/enemies, edit its texture/frame counts/tint/fps, and assign it to an enemy archetype registration. Standalone scenes expose one appearance for F6 preview. This changes presentation only. Binding validates required styles/components and rejects incomplete scenes.

For different health, speed, radius or weapon mechanics, edit the corresponding Resource under data. scripts/content.odin uses Replay's definition baker to validate a complete catalog and rejects duplicate IDs or invalid fields with source paths. The baked catalog is a value in World and recovery checkpoints. Editing a Resource afterward cannot mutate a running simulation. Reopen a run to admit a new catalog. Export the same typed bake with tools/stock.py --project PATH for headless stock/tests; --check detects stale content. Snapshots carry the host's catalog. Semantic code/schema changes still follow the game's version/conversion policy.

For new behavior, add explicit owned component state if necessary, implement its pure tick/action rule, validate it, and expose any authoring configuration through Resource baking. Add the required display fields/projection and let an appropriate view component render them. Cosmetic child composition alone needs no wire change. A new enemy kind needs a stable gameplay ID, explicit behavior and one authored archetype registration; attaching a script to a Node does not automatically register multiplayer gameplay.

Identities, input, and recovery#

Enemies and loot follow entity generations. New generations and epoch/reset/floor boundaries start new view lifetimes. Initial observations establish comparison values without emitting effects. Runners are four permanent seat views; generation/warp/epoch changes reset local body cues while preserving seat/node identity for camera and UI references. Their lifetimes therefore differ from the entity-generation lifetimes used by enemies and loot.

Movement/held controls and discrete actions retain their existing admission paths. Scene/UI signals can request actions; they do not mutate World. Local player poses use prediction and smoothing, remote actors use observed presentation, and permission checks use authority state. Camera following preserves the authoritative roster and matches the displayed body's generation.

Client wound effects use exact retained public event-tick frames because ordinary snapshots omit the server's hit_history. Such frames may contain corrected or locally predicted poses; they are cosmetic placement, not hit evidence. Missing ticks or a mismatched generation refuse placement. Authority hit judgment/history remain intact.

Procedural rendering and specialized paths#

Seeded arena dressing, projectile/beam/glob batches, particles/trails and some presentation-service orchestration remain procedural. Their geometry or membership is generated or changes frequently. Earlier performance comparisons measured a cost when replacing preallocated slots with per-lifetime scenes. Audio routing, lobby/shop signals and existing authored menu/HUD scenes retain their appropriate APIs. These paths own rendering state separately from gameplay. Scene properties remain appropriate for authored appearance; procedural batches remain appropriate for generated geometry.

This page describes the example's ownership and composition workflow. Older features and the historical parity ledger remain in the project, and specialized rendering paths can have different requirements.

Validation#

Shell
REPLAY_EDITOR_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output \
  nix develop --command bash tests/replay_editor/run.sh

The gate builds an isolated project, checks native/WASM script compilation, independent scene previews, edited child offsets/Resources, script/component rejection, catalog baking, actor/feedback/audio/HUD behavior, and combat/revive host-client-observer agreement. Recovery/performance receipts and exact limits are recorded in the delivery assessment. No original game or simulation schema is replaced by this workflow.
